source.snippet: I manage a travel website that provides visa assistance services for UAE residents. The website has multiple country-specific pages targeting searches such as visa services from Dubai, Schengen visa applications, and tourist visa guides. Some pages perform well in Google search results, while others receive very little organic traffic despite having detailed content. I have already worked on: Creating unique content for each visa service page, Adding internal links between related articles...

problem_statement: Operators of niche travel and visa-assistance websites serving specific regional markets (e.g. UAE outbound) cannot identify why identical SEO tactics produce inconsistent rankings across country-specific service pages, leading to wasted content investment and uneven revenue.
target_segment: Small travel agency and visa-assistance website operators in GCC/MENA region targeting outbound travel searches
notes: Buyer context: commercial website operator with revenue tied to organic traffic; already investing in SEO work (content, internal links, schema). Explicit business context—visa assistance is a paid service. Pain is inconsistent SEO ROI across a portfolio of similar pages. A page-level SEO audit tool that benchmarks country-specific travel/visa pages against each other and surfaces differentiation gaps could command a subscription from agencies in this vertical.
